idiom_name: class DirView(raw: Dir, m: Membrane) with export clauses and mediated overrides
implementation_notes: Scala 3 generates forwarding members at compile time: an export clause makes the members of another object available under the wrapper's name (`export raw.open as rawOpen`, or a selector list for several members), so the classic forwarding boilerplate disappears and the compiler still type-checks every forwarded member (docs.scala-lang.org). The membrane is a class holding the raw capability whose exported members are unmediated and whose own definitions override the ones that must be mediated, wrapping arguments and results by hand. Use it when the mediated surface is known and should fail loudly at compile time; use the Dynamic variant when the surface is large, open or assembled at run time, and the JVM dynamic proxy when every call - including equals/hashCode - must land in one handler.
code_sketch:
final class DirView(raw: Dir, m: Membrane) extends Dir:
  export raw.open as rawOpen            // forwarded member, unmediated

  def open(path: String): File =        // same name: the mediated override wins
    if m.revoked then throw IllegalStateException("revoked")
    else m.wrap(rawOpen(path))          // wrap the way out

  export raw.*                          // rest of the surface forwards as-is
pitfalls: Exported members are unmediated: a class that exports the whole surface and overrides some members has exactly the overridden ones mediated, with no runtime hook to catch the rest.

An export creates a new member rather than delegating dynamically, so references to the wrapper and to the target are distinct for identity and equality checks - keep a per-membrane identity map if the application compares references.

Export requires a stable path and forwards at the call site's compile time: a target that must be swapped on revocation cannot be re-pointed through an export, which is where Dynamic or a JVM proxy is the better hook.

variants.name: scala.Dynamic (selectDynamic/applyDynamic) for total mediation
variants.idiom_name: membrane extending scala.Dynamic, rewriting unsupported selections to selectDynamic/applyDynamic
variants.implementation_notes: A class extending scala.Dynamic gets a compile-time rewriting rule: any selection or invocation the type checker cannot resolve becomes selectDynamic("name") or applyDynamic("name")(args...) instead of a compile error, so one method can mediate an entire surface, known or not (scala-lang.org API). The membrane is then a Dynamic wrapper holding the raw capability that checks revocation, wraps the arguments, forwards by reflective or explicit dispatch and wraps the result - the total-mediation property the export variant cannot have. The cost is that every mediated call is unchecked at compile time and the call site needs the `import scala.language.dynamics` opt-in, so this variant suits dynamic, open surfaces rather than fixed interfaces.
pitfalls: Dynamic rewriting only happens for selections the type checker cannot resolve: a member that actually exists on the static type is called directly and never reaches selectDynamic, so declaring the interface on the wrapper reopens a raw route.
Everything crossing the dynamic boundary is Any and unchecked: argument and result types must be validated by hand, and reflective invocation wraps target exceptions in InvocationTargetException.
Call sites need import scala.language.dynamics, and identity semantics change because the wrapper is a distinct object - both must be handled deliberately.
